questions.prompt: How do you declare a class that inherits from another class in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, the colon (:) syntax is used for inheritance. 'public class Derived : Base' means Derived inherits from Base, also called the derived class and base class respectively.

What is the purpose of the 'base' keyword in a derived class constructor?
options: To create a new instance of the base class
To call the base class constructor before the derived constructor body runs
To cast to the base class type
To inherit the base class fields
questions.explanation: The 'base' keyword in a constructor—': base(args)'—explicitly calls a specific base class constructor before the derived constructor's body executes. If omitted, the parameterless base constructor is called automatically.

Which statement about inheritance is false?
options: C# supports multiple inheritance of classes.
A derived class inherits members from its base class.
You can prevent inheritance by sealing a class.
Constructors are not inherited, but their effects are seen through base() calls.
questions.explanation: C# does NOT support multiple inheritance of classes (a class can have only one direct base class). You can achieve multiple interface inheritance, but not multiple class inheritance. The other statements are all true.
